note: Sample recalls: fictional, for the Remedy demo only. Brightline Home is a fictional sample firm, and BH-2026-01 is not a CPSC recall number. Kept apart from recalls.json, so no CPSC statistic, explorer count or benchmark ever includes them. Photos: one real laptop charger before and after its cord was cut, by Dmitry G on Wikimedia Commons (public domain, PD-self); see public/samples/charger/CREDITS.json. The charger's maker has not recalled it, and its brand marks and label text were removed for the demo.

recalls.title: Brightline Home recalls 65W laptop chargers (sample recall)
recalls.hazard: The charger's cord can overheat where it meets the case, posing a fire hazard.
recalls.remedyText: Stop using the charger and cut the power cord where it meets the charger case. Send one photo of the cut cord with the charger for a full refund of $34.99.

explanation.plain: Unplug the charger and cut its cord where it meets the case. Send one photo of the cut cord with the charger to get $34.99 back.
explanation.technical: Written by hand by the sample firm, no model call. "cut the power cord where it meets the charger case" sets cut_cord; "one photo of the cut cord with the charger" sets whole_product and cut_or_damage; "a full refund of $34.99" sets full_refund and refund_amount 34.99; claims come through Remedy's web form.
